items.question: Under what condition must that which is to be concealed be guarded with effort in the mortal world among the lowest of men?
premises: Concealment is required in the mortal world.
Effort is the means for such concealment.
This duty falls especially among the lowest of men.
items.inference: What is to be concealed demands effortful protection in that setting.
uncertainties: Scope of what is to be concealed remains unspecified.
items.plain_english: What is to be concealed must be guarded with effort in the mortal world, among the lowest of men.

items.question: What kind of prior accomplishment must be given only after it has been tested for one year?
premises: A prior accomplishment is a candidate for giving.
Such a candidate must undergo testing.
The required test duration is one year.
items.inference: Only a prior accomplishment tested for one year is fit to be given.
uncertainties: The identity of the recipient is not specified.
items.plain_english: What was accomplished before is to be given only after it has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter is identified as the fifth to have emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: A chapter emerged from Candradvīpa.
That chapter holds a fixed ordinal position.
Its position is the fifth.
items.inference: The fifth chapter is the one that emerged from Candradvīpa.
uncertainties: No content of the chapter is indicated here.
items.plain_english: The fifth chapter is the one that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By whose grace does the speaker come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of the Kaulas.
Knowledge arises by that lord's grace.
What becomes known is the determination of the Kaula teaching.
items.inference: By the grace of the lord of the Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the Kaula determination.
uncertainties: The prior state of ignorance is not detailed.
items.plain_english: By your grace, O lord of the Kaulas, I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What claim is at stake in determining whether the declared soul is a distinct entity or identical with its own nature?
premises: A soul is said to be declared.
It is asked who that soul is.
It is asked what its nature is or whether nature is meant.
items.inference: The question seeks to distinguish the soul as entity from its nature.
uncertainties: No answer is given in this verse.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared? Or what is the nature of the soul?

rows.grounds: interrogative pronoun with fused ending as given

items.question: What claim about dissolution is at stake in asking where all of that goes to dissolution and to be told so?
premises: All that is said to go to dissolution.
The locus of that dissolution is in question.
The speaker requests that the whole matter be told.
items.inference: Knowledge of the locus of dissolution is sought for all that dissolves.
uncertainties: The referent of 'all that' is not specified here.
items.plain_english: And indeed, in what does all that go to dissolution? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What claim is at stake in identifying that which is supreme as partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless?
premises: A single referent is indicated.
That referent is supreme.
That referent is characterized as partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.
items.inference: The supreme reality is characterized by negation of parts, change, affliction, and stain.
uncertainties: The ontological status relative to the soul is not settled here.
items.plain_english: He is the supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease and stainless one.

items.question: What claim is at stake in identifying the soul as more supreme than something else while also identifying it as the Haṃsa who is power and individual?
premises: The soul is said to be more supreme.
A relative clause identifies that referent.
That same referent is called the Haṃsa, power and individual.
items.inference: The soul is identified with the Haṃsa understood as power and individual, and as more supreme.
uncertainties: The term of comparison for 'more supreme' is not stated here.
items.plain_english: He is the soul, more supreme. Indeed, he is the Haṃsa, power and individual.

items.question: What claim is at stake in holding that the wind-filling air is situated in all beings?
premises: There is an air described as wind-filling.
That air is present in all beings.
Its presence is described as situated there.
items.inference: The wind-filling air pervades and is situated in all beings.
uncertainties: The mode of its situatedness is not specified.
items.plain_english: The wind-filling air is situated in all beings.

items.question: What claim is at stake in holding that upon merely leaving the body one is called the supreme Śiva?
premises: A referent is indicated.
The condition is merely leaving the body.
Under that condition that referent is called the supreme Śiva.
items.inference: Merely leaving the body is said to be the condition for being called the supreme Śiva.
uncertainties: Whether this is a status attained or recognized is not clear.
items.plain_english: He, upon merely leaving the body, is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: What claim is at stake in holding that what abides in the ear is heard as something that has come down through a traditional order?
premises: Something abiding in the ear is heard.
That thing is addressed in relation to the goddess.
It is described as having come down through a traditional order.
items.inference: What is heard in the ear is transmitted through a traditional order.
uncertainties: The content of what is heard is not specified.
items.plain_english: O goddess, what abides in the ear is heard as that which has come down through tradition in order.

items.question: What claim is at stake in holding that by this mere knowledge, and by what has been heard, a result follows for the one addressed?
premises: A means is indicated as mere knowledge.
What has been heard is added as a further means.
The address is to one of fair face.
items.inference: Mere knowledge together with what has been heard is presented as a sufficient means here.
uncertainties: The specific result is not stated in this verse.
items.plain_english: By this mere knowledge, and by what has been heard, O fair-faced one.

rows.grounds: ablative of ṣaṇmāsa with fused ending as given

items.question: What claim is at stake in holding that one who practices for six months should wear an ochre robe free from bondage?
premises: A practice is to be undertaken for six months.
The practitioner is indicated by a relative clause.
That practitioner should wear an ochre robe described as free from bondage.
items.inference: After or in the course of six months of practice, wearing an ochre robe free from bondage is enjoined.
uncertainties: The causal link between practice and the robe is not explicit.
items.plain_english: Whoever should practice for six months, indeed, should wear an ochre robe free from bondage.

items.question: What claim is at stake in holding that one freed from all diseases attains union together with yogis?
premises: A state of being freed from all diseases is posited.
Association with yogis is indicated.
Union together with them is the result stated.
items.inference: Freedom from all diseases is linked to union together with yogis.
uncertainties: The nature of that union is not specified.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with yogis.

items.question: What claim is at stake in holding that the practice of the soul has been told to the one addressed?
premises: Something is indicated as this.
That something is the practice of the soul.
It has been told to the addressed one, O Bhairavī.
items.inference: The practice of the soul is now declared to Bhairavī.
uncertainties: No details of the practice are given in this verse.
items.plain_english: This practice of the soul has been told to you, and to you, O Bhairavī.

items.question: What claim is at stake in restricting giving to one who is endowed with all states and of resolved mind?
premises: A gift is said to be to be given.
The recipient is described as endowed with all states.
The recipient is also described as one of resolved mind.
items.inference: Only one endowed with all states and of resolved mind is fit to receive what is to be given.
uncertainties: What is to be given is not specified here.
items.plain_english: It is to be given to one endowed with all states, to one of resolved mind.

items.question: What claim is at stake in forbidding the giving of the Kaula essence to those of yoginī origin?
premises: The Kaula essence is a candidate for giving.
A restriction is introduced by negation.
That restriction applies with regard to those of yoginī origin.
items.inference: The Kaula essence is not to be given to those of yoginī origin.
uncertainties: The reason for the restriction is not stated here.
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence is not to be given, indeed, to those of yoginī origin.

items.question: What claim is at stake in contrasting the speaker's body as pure today with its being struck by a veil of ignorance?
premises: The speaker refers to their own body.
The body is described as pure.
That same body is described as struck by a veil of ignorance.
items.inference: A tension is posited between the body's purity and its being struck by a veil of ignorance.
uncertainties: The temporal resolution of this tension is not stated.
items.plain_english: Today my pure body is struck by a veil of ignorance.

items.question: What claim is at stake in the speaker's wish to hear now of the auspicious deception of time?
premises: The speaker wishes to hear something now.
The object is the deception of time.
That deception is described as auspicious.
items.inference: The speaker seeks knowledge of time's auspicious deception.
uncertainties: How deception can be auspicious is not explained here.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear of the auspicious deception of time.

items.question: What claim is at stake in asserting without doubt that death is destroyed in the manner to be told?
premises: The speaker states an intention to tell.
Doubt is denied.
The claim is that death is destroyed.
items.inference: A method by which death is destroyed is to be told, and that claim admits no doubt.
uncertainties: The manner of destruction is not given in this verse.
items.plain_english: I tell it; there is no doubt that death is destroyed as such.

items.question: What claim is at stake in holding that even a wise person, while burning, acts at the tip of nectar with the tip of essence?
premises: An action is directed to the tip of nectar.
It is done with the tip of essence.
The agent is even a wise person while burning.
items.inference: A practice involving the tip of nectar and essence is possible even for a wise person in a burning state.
uncertainties: The purpose of the action is not stated here.
items.plain_english: At the tip of nectar, with the tip of essence, even a wise person, while burning, does so.

items.question: What claim is at stake in enjoining that air be placed at the root of the tongue and palate and drunk slowly?
premises: A location is specified at the root of the tongue and palate.
Air is to be made there.
That air is to be drunk slowly.
items.inference: A slow practice of drawing or drinking air at that location is enjoined.
uncertainties: The physiological or yogic effect is not stated here.
items.plain_english: Having made the air at the root of the tongue and palate, one should drink it slowly.

rows.grounds: compound = yadā+abhyasta; nominative/accusative as given with fused ending

items.question: What claim is at stake in holding that when this practice has been done for one year, old age and death are destroyed?
premises: A practice is undertaken for one year.
That practice is described as having been practiced.
Old age and death are said to be destroyed under that condition.
items.inference: One year of this practice is said to destroy old age and death.
uncertainties: The exact practice referred to is not repeated here.
items.plain_english: When it has been practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What claim is at stake in holding that poison does not enter the body even if one has been bitten by great serpents?
premises: A bite by great serpents is posited.
Poison is the usual agent in such a bite.
It is claimed that poison does not enter the body in that case.
items.inference: Under the condition established by the prior practice, poison does not enter the body even from bites by great serpents.
uncertainties: The condition from prior verses is presupposed but not repeated here.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
